title: Advanced Materials Characterization
requirements: For students in MSc Advanced Materials Science
description: This course covers principles, operation and data analysis skills of most useful advanced materials characterization techniques in modern research, with X-ray, electron, and ion beam as probing sources. The content includes surface spectroscopy, diffraction, electron microscopy, mass spectroscopy and etc.
outcome: 1. Master the principle of commonly used materials characterization and analytical techniques2. Interpret experimental results obtained by the materials characterization techniques covered in the course3. Apply the concepts and methodology in materials characterization in realistic problems and cases4. Analyze, judge and solve realistic problems and cases in relation to materials characterization5. Develop an analytical mind towards materials characterization
syllabus: Surface characterizationElectron microscopyDiffractionChromatographyMass spectroscopyParticle beam techniques

recommended_readings: Lecture notes and related reading materials will be provided by course instructors.

title: Advanced Materials Synthesis
requirements: For students in MSc Advanced Materials Science
description: This course introduces the fabrication methods of traditional materials (including metals, ceramics and polymers) and advanced materials (including nanomaterials, semiconductors, smart materials, biomaterials, and so on). Students will learn basic scientific principles involved in the synthesis, processing, scaling up, and quality control. Frontier synthetic methodologies, such as those involving theoretical predictions or cutting-edge fabrication techniques, will also be introduced.
outcome: 1. To learn the classification of traditional and advanced materials, understand their basic building blocks, and appreciate the importance of structure-property in Materials Science. 2. To know the various fabrication methods for traditional and advanced materials. 3. Via case studies of representative advanced materials, to understand the fundamentals in advanced materials synthesis. 4. To learn various advanced aiding tools for materials fabrication.5. To understand basic principles of quality control.
syllabus: Topic 1: Classification of Materials (10%)Topic 2: Fabrication Methods of Traditional Materials (30%)Topic 3: Synthetic Methods of Representative Advanced Materials (50%)Topic 4: Introduction to Quality Control (10%)
required_readings: Lecture notes and related reading materials will be provided by course instructors.
recommended_readings: Lecture notes and related reading materials will be provided by course instructors.

title: Frontiers in Advanced Materials
requirements: For students in MSc Advanced Materials Science
description: This course offers a comprehensive exploration of various types of advanced materials across diverse fields, such as energy materials, biomaterials, photonic materials, quantum materials, chiral materials, optoelectronic materials, etc. Through lectures, case studies, and discussions, students will gain insights into the role of these materials in driving technological innovation and addressing global challenges.
outcome: Students at the end of the course are expected to have gained an appreciation of the fundamental concepts as well as the state-of-the-art methodologies in frontiers of materials research. They are expected to have gained the ability to operate these concepts in precise frameworks, and to have the ability to pursue these topics in further depth beyond this course. Some of the material will have to be learnt by the students on their own, and through this activity students will develop the capability and habit of self-directed learning.

(~ 2 weeks)2. Energy storage materials (battery), electrochemical principles, present development and challenges. (~ 1 week)3. Plasmonic materials, including their synthesis, characterization, properties, and diverse applications. (~ 2 weeks)4. Mechanical and Hydrodynamic Metamaterials. (1 week)5. Semiconducting materials, surface, defect and doping. (1 week)6. Photovoltaic materials, fundamental mechanism, device fabrication, and research frontiers (1 week)7. Organic electronics: Introduction to organic electronics with a case study on molecular engineering of organic field effect transistors (2 weeks)8. Nanomaterials: phase engineering, chiral nanomaterials and various applications (1 week)9. Polymer and biopolymer materials: synthesis, properties, and applications in health (1 week)10. Materials for application in photocatalysis (1 week)

title: AI-Driven Materials Design and Simulations
requirements: For students in MSc Advanced Materials Science
description: The course provides a basic introduction to artificial intelligence (AI) approaches in materials design and simulations. It covers machine learning (ML) techniques, data-driven materials design and searches in large materials databases, and AI-assisted materials simulations. Students will gain foundational knowledge and hands-on experience using AI and simulations to predict material properties, design novel materials, and address real-world materials design challenges.
outcome: 1.  Understand fundamental principles of artificial intelligence applied to materials design and simulations.2.  Apply AI-related concepts and approaches to basic materials research problems.3.  Interpret and analyze results from AI-assisted materials modeling and simulations.4.  Enhance the understanding of general concepts in materials simulations and data-driven modeling.5.  Develop an analytical mindset toward AI-driven materials research.
syllabus: 1.  Basic concepts and introduction to artificial intelligence in materials science2.  Data, databases, and data-driven materials modeling3.  AI-assisted materials simulations4.  Applications and case studies in materials design5.  Current challenges and future perspectives
required_readings: Lecture notes and related reading materials will be provided by course instructors.
recommended_readings: Lecture notes and related reading materials will be provided by course instructors.

title: Properties of Advanced Materials
requirements: For students in MSc Advanced Materials Science
description: The course provides an in-depth exploration of selected properties and applications of advanced materials. It starts with an introductory module covering the essential concepts and ideas in quantum physics for studying advanced materials. It is followed by modules on semiconductors, heterostructures and their applications; magnetic properties and materials; and superconducting materials and applications. Students will be exposed to a balanced discussion among the basic principles, materials, applications, and the latest developments.
outcome: 1. To acquire basic concepts in quantum physics and apply them to study atoms, bonding, energy bands, and conducting, insulating and semiconducting materials.2. To acquire the basic principles, properties of selected materials, applications, and latest developments in semiconductors, superconductors, and magnetic materials. 3. To develop an awareness of the impact of advanced materials in the years to come.4. To develop an awareness of the research opportunities offered by advanced materials and to motivate life-long learning.
syllabus: Basic quantum physics for materials studiesTopics include - Electron waves, Schrodinger equation, confinement and energy levels, tunnelling, atoms, bonding in molecules, from bonds to bands, free electron waves in metals, density of states, filling in electrons, bands and band gaps, metals, insulators and semiconductors.Semiconductors, heterostructures and their applicationsTopics include – bands and band alignment, doping, p-n junction, two-dimensional electron gas, quantum Hall effect, quantum cascade laser, split gate technology, quantum dots.Magnetic Properties, materials, and applicationsTopics include – orbital and spin magnetic dipole moments, paramagnetism, diamagnetism, ferromagnetism and anti-ferromagnetism, experimental methods, giant magnetoresistance, spin-transfer torque, domains and domain wall motion, spin current and spin-orbit torque, magnetic tunnel junctions, and topics in non-colinear and unconventional magnets. Superconductivity: Principles, materials, and applicationsTopics include – zero resistance and Meissner effect, London equations and penetration depth, Type I and Type II superconductors, Cooper pairs and energy gap, role of Fermi surface, phase transition viewpoint, low Tc and high Tc materials, cryogenics and measurement techniques, selected applications, hydrides superconductors and other frontier topics.
required_readings: Lecture notes and reading materials will be provided by the teachers of the modules.
recommended_readings: Lecture notes and reading materials will be provided by the teachers of the modules.

title: Functional Molecules for Optoelectronics
requirements: For students in MSc Advanced Materials Science
description: This course provides an overview of functional molecules for applications in organic (opto)electronic devices including organic field-effect transistors (OFETs), organic solar cells (OSCs), organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs), and organic photodetectors. It covers the design of functional molecules, device architectures, and key physical properties such as light absorption, luminescence, electrical conductivity, and magnetic behavior. The course also introduces essential principles of organic and supramolecular chemistry underpinning advances in organic optoelectronics.
outcome: 1. Understand the electronic structures of organic molecular materials and band structures of solid-state materials.2. Understand the photo-physical properties and electronic conductivities of organic materials. 3. Understand the working principle, device structures of Organic Light-Emitting Diode (OLED), Organic Field-Effect Transistor (OFET) and Organic Solar Cell (OSC). 4. Understand the basic organic chemistry and supramolecular chemistry principles for developing organic electronic materials, and apply these principles to explain the structures, properties and functions of functional molecules in organic (opto)electronics.
syllabus: Chapter 1: Organic Semiconductor Materials, Electronic Structures, Atomic and Molecular OrbitalsChapter 2: Basic Photophysical Parameters and Spectroscopic MethodsChapter 3: Excited Molecules, Optical Process (Energy Transfer and Exciton Diffusion) in Organic SemiconductorChapter 4: Fermi Level and Band Structure. Electrical Current and Carrier Transport.Chapter 5: Charge Carrier Recombination, Dissociation of ExcitationsChapter 6: Device structure and operational principle of OLED, OFET and OSCChapter 7: Organic chemistry of polycyclic arenes for organic electronic materialsChapter 8: Supramolecular chemistry for organic electronic materialsChapter 9: Molecular switches and devices
required_readings: Lecture notes and related reading materials will be provided by course instructors.
recommended_readings: Lecture notes and related reading materials will be provided by course instructors.

title: Biomaterials for Healthcare
requirements: For students in MSc Advanced Materials Science
description: This course will cover the fundamentals of biomaterials, including the chemistry of proteins, carbohydrates and lipids, and the advanced applications of biomaterials in tissue engineering and regeneration. Examples of healthcare products, including collagen-based biomaterials, will be described.
outcome: 1. To learn the basic composition of biomaterials.2. To promote and advance a molecular view of biomaterials. 3. To appreciate the priority of safety in the practical application of biomaterials. 4. To understand the rigorous regulation of biomaterials. 5. To gain basic knowledge on biomaterial industry and to understand the job opportunity and requirement of working in biomaterials.
syllabus: Chapter 1: Classes of Materials Used in MedicineChapter 2: Background Concepts in the Use of Biomaterials in Surgery and Medical DevicesChapter 3: Host Reaction to Biomaterials and Their Evaluation Chapter 4: Biological Testing of BiomaterialsChapter 5: Degradation of Materials in the Biological EnvironmentChapter 6: Applications of Biomaterials in Functional Tissue EngineeringChapter 7: Implants, Devices, and Biomaterials: Special ConsiderationsChapter 8: Voluntary Standards, Regulatory Compliance, and Non-Technical Issues

recommended_readings: Lecture notes and related reading materials will be provided by course instructors.

title: Surface Science and Thin Film Technology
requirements: For students in MSc Advanced Materials Science
description: This course introduces surface science, the fabrication, characterization, and physical properties of thin films. The topics include vacuum science and technology, basic concepts of surface science, thin film deposition techniques, kinetics and thermodynamics of surface reactions, film growth processes and modes, characterization, epitaxy, and physical properties of thin films. State-of-the-art research advancements on thin film preparation and properties are also selectively introduced.
outcome: (1) To learn the basic principles of surface science.(2) To know the technologies that are related to thin films.(3) To understand the basic principles of vacuum science and technology that are related to surface science and thin-film deposition techniques.(4) To understand the thermodynamics of evaporation and learn the basic principles of evaporation.(5) To acquire the basic knowledge about adsorption, surface diffusion, nucleation, and structure development that are involved in thin-film deposition.(6) To acquire the basic knowledge of epitaxial deposition.(7) To learn the basic knowledge of chemical vapor deposition.(8) To learn the basic techniques of measuring the physical and chemical properties of thin films.
syllabus: 1: Introduction to Surface Science and Thin Film Technology2: Vacuum Science and Technology3: Surface Science4: Evaporation5: Deposition6: Epitaxy7: Chemical Vapor Deposition8: Analysis and Properties of Thin Films

title: Functional Materials for Clean Energy and Sustainability
requirements: For students in MSc Advanced Materials Science
description: This interdisciplinary course explores the design, synthesis, and application of advanced functional materials critical to address global energy and environmental challenges. Students will learn how cutting-edge materials science drives innovations in renewable energy technologies, energy storage, carbon capture and green chemistry. The course integrates the principles of chemistry, physics, and materials science to prepare students for careers in research, industry, or policy-making in clean energy and sustainability.
outcome: 1. To learn the core concepts and methodologies in the design and characterization of functional materials for sustainable development through thematic lectures. 2. To establish a systematic framework of thinking for understanding the structure–property–performance relationships of materials, and to analyze and design innovative materials for renewable energy and green technologies. 3. To utilize advanced characterization techniques (such as spectroscopy and microscopy) to visualize and interpret the micro-structural and chemical features of materials. 4. To cultivate rigorous scientific attitudes, critical thinking, and independent research abilities to address complex challenges in clean energy and sustainable technologies. 5. To develop the ability of critically evaluating application potentials of materials in energy and environmental systems, recognizing that even theoretically superior materials may face challenges in scalability, economic feasibility, and long-term stability, and remaining aware of the limitations and discrepancies between experimental results, material models, and real-world conditions.
syllabus: Chapter 1: Introduction to Functional Materials and Sustainable EnergyChapter 2: Synthesis and Characterization of Advanced Functional MaterialsChapter 3: Green Chemistry and Environmental Functional MaterialsChapter 4: Frontiers and Interdisciplinary Topics in Sustainable Materials- Materials for Carbon Capture, Utilization, and Storage (CCUS)- Materials for Photoelectrochemical Energy Conversion- Materials for Chemical Energy Storage and Battery- Materials for Thermoelectric and Catalytic Conversion

title: Electronics and Photonics
requirements: For students in MSc Advanced Materials Science
description: This course is devoted to the fundamental concepts, structures, and working principles of common electronic and photonic devices. It includes the fundamental concepts of semiconductors, field-effect transistors, Schottky junctions, p-n junctions, light-emitting diodes, lasers, photodetectors, solar cells, waveguides, and control of light polarization. Closely related materials and state-of-the-art research advancements on electronics and photonics are also selectively introduced.
outcome: (1) To acquire the basic knowledge of semiconductor physics.(2) To learn field-effect transistors and Schottky junctions.(3) To learn the working principles of dielectric waveguides and optical fibers and related materials.(4) To learn pn junctions.(5) To learn the working principle of light-emitting diodes and related semiconductor materials.(6) To learn the working principle of laser diodes.(7) To learn the working principle of photodetectors.(8) To learn the working principle of solar cells and related materials.
syllabus: 1. Introduction2. Semiconductor Physics I3. Semiconductor Physics II4. Field-effect transistors and Schottky junctions5. Dielectric Waveguides and Optical Fibers6. pn Junction I7. pn Junction II8. Light-Emitting Diodes9. Laser Diodes10. Photodetectors11. Photovoltaic Devices
